Analysis: Both hypotheses offer innovative strategies combining metabolic modulation with immune reprogramming to treat HCC. Hypothesis 1 proposes a dual-target approach by inhibiting MAT to blunt SAM/MTA production and concurrently blocking the CXCL11/CXCR3 axis, using established cutting‐edge techniques such as CRISPR-Cas9 and single-cell transcriptomics. This approach, while complex, is built on clearer mechanistic foundations and uses interventions that are more directly testable and better aligned with safety considerations, provided targeted delivery can be achieved. In contrast, Hypothesis 2 centers on a nanotechnology-based delivery system to target methionine metabolism along with broader metabolic disruptions, making it novel but adding extra layers of complexity. The nanodelivery system raises additional uncertainties regarding targeting specificity, biodistribution, and potential off-target effects, which may compromise both plausibility and safety. Overall, Hypothesis 1 is superior in terms of novelty, plausibility, testability, and safety.
